corpus_findings.detail: An inverted verdict with no control block. The PASS is computed correctly from the evidence; the evidence just cannot distinguish 'did not fire' from 'could not be seen'. method/12 G1.

fragment_A.why: Both outputs are required. The verdict stays PASS because the evaluator judges evidence, not specification quality — the corpus finding is how the gate learns to reject this statically instead.

fragment_D.why: The inverted assertion is true and the verdict is still FAIL. The bracket failed, so the clean absence poll covers an unknown fraction of the window — 'the event did not fire' collapses into 'nothing could have been seen to fire'.

conformance_note: Fragments C and D differ only in the trailing control. An evaluator that returns the same verdict for both has treated the bracket as decoration, and every inverted scenario it evaluates is a front-only control — proof the pipeline was live when the window opened and nothing more.
